Subscribers get unlimited access to exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hi. Bonjour. Welcome to our live report on for the elite women's road race on the final weekend of the 2026 UCI World Road Championships in Montréal, Canada.September 26, 2026 – 8:37 AMReigning champion Magdeleine Vallieres of Canada shared her thoughts on social media on the eve of the road race.September 26, 2026 – 8:42 AMWill Dutch racer Demi Vollering finally win a world title today? She lines up as the top favourite, having swept almost all before her this season.September 26, 2026 – 8:52 AMMore on Vollering from Laurens ten Dam, the Dutch team coach: "She is incredibly focused, that's true. Two days after the Tour de France, I got the first message already from her, 'OK, job's not finished'. I was like, 'OK, she's on'," Ten Dam told on Thursday evening.'Job's not finished' – Demi Vollering keeping quiet on game plan as she leads Dutch squad at Road World ChampionshipsTwo-time Tour de France Femmes winner thrives on responsibility this year as lone team leader for first rainbow rewardSeptember 26, 2026 – 8:55 AMAlong with Vallieres, Belgian leader Lotte Kopecky is the only previous World Champion lining up at the start. She won twice before, in Glasgow in 2023 and Zurich in 2024.Speaking on Friday, Kopecky acknowledged that Demi Vollering stands out as the favourite, but said plenty of other contenders are in the mix.'She might well be the woman to beat' – Lotte Kopecky acknowledges Demi Vollering is top World Championships favourite but points to strong field of contenders'If that top day comes, then a lot is possible' says two-time world champion of her own chances in MontrealSeptember 26, 2026 – 8:58 AMThree minutes until the start in Brossard - more on the route coming up.It is sunny in Brossard, with cool temperatures around 12°C, but the day should warm up, as the forecast calls for a high of 23°C in Montréal.September 26, 2026 – 8:59 AMThe 140 riders representing 57 nations, including new countries of Panama, the Philippines and Saudi Arabia are off.They will face 2570 metres of elevation gain over the 180.4km course featuring the closing Mount Royal circuit.September 26, 2026 – 9:08 AMStarting on the South Shore in Brossard, the women head south on an approximately 43km loop through Carignan, Chambly, and Richelieu in the Montérégie region before returning to Brossard and heading to Montréal.The peloton will then ride the Samuel-De Champlain Bridge towards the Mount Royal circuit which the women will tackle eight times, after having 73km in the legs already. The now-iconic circuit features several major challenges: the Voie Camillien-Houde, the Chemin de la Polytechnique, and the tough false flat rising along Avenue du Parc to the line.September 26, 2026 – 9:10 AMThe flag drops, and the race is on after a 4km neutral section. Peloton is spread across the road with the Dutch team massed at the front.September 26, 2026 – 9:13 AMMischael Alhazmi from Saudi Arabia is the first attacker but is quickly back in the peloton.September 26, 2026 – 9:19 AMLots of chatter in the peloton as they roll by fans on the side of the road.September 26, 2026 – 9:22 AMCanada's Maggie Coles-Lyster and Alison Jackson are at the front and in the middle of the peloton, controlling things for now for their teammate, defending champion Vallieres Mill.September 26, 2026 – 9:33 AMGreece’s Argyro Milaki and Israel’s Rotem Gafinovitz attack out of a right-hand turn and get a small gap with 166km to go.Six riders try to come across to the head of the race.September 26, 2026 – 9:34 AMOne of the riders trying to come across to the duo was Canada's Alison Jackson, and the move is nullified. September 26, 2026 – 9:36 AMAnother attack by Gafinovitz with Antri Christoforou (Cyprus) jumps on, but once again, the move is shut down. Portugal's Beatriz Rosso counters solo, and there is no immediate reaction from the pelotonSeptember 26, 2026 – 9:41 AMMore riders jump from the peloton and make it across the 15-second gap to Rosso. The move includes Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), and Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria)September 26, 2026 – 9:44 AMTallest rider in the peloton, Teniel Campbell (Trinidad & Tobago) attacks to bridge across and that gets an immediate reaction from Alison Jackson. Jackson seems to be trying to get into a break and the peloton, led by the Dutch team, shuts that down immediately.September 26, 2026 – 9:47 AMCampbell is not giving up, as she attacks once again, and more riders jump on her wheel. But the peloton doesn't want more riders to join the four riders in the break and Campbell can't escape.September 26, 2026 – 9:49 AMFour riders made it into the break, initiated by Beatriz Rosso (Portugal) with 162 km to go, and she was joined by Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), and Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria). The quartet have 44 seconds with 154km to go. September 26, 2026 – 9:54 AMAnother rider tries to jump to the break but the Dutch team reels her back in. They don't want to let any other rider to join the move.September 26, 2026 – 9:59 AMThe Dutch team is lined up at the front of the peloton, with some wind impacting the riders, controlling the gap, now up 1:40 to the break.September 26, 2026 – 10:01 AMA crash takes down riders on the left side of the road. Riders going down included Adèle Normand (Canada) and Sandrine Tas (Belgium).Normand gets up quickly and is back on her bike, while Tas had to wait for her mechanic to sort out her bike.September 26, 2026 – 10:03 AMAs the peloton seems happy with the break composition, let's hear what defending Magdeleine Vallieres Mill had to say at the start this morning.“It [having the rainbow jersey] changed a lot. I mean, it's been such an honour this year to be able to wear the jersey and to be able to come back here at home and with the number one with a really good team. So yeah, it's been super special.“We're gonna try [to keep the title]. I think we have, yeah, a super strong team, so we're gonna give it a go.”September 26, 2026 – 10:06 AMAfter going to her team car, Normand stops to quickly switch one shoe that the mechanic brought to her from the car. Nicely done. With no team radios, she calmly went to the car to let them, and give time for the mechanic to get her shoe out of her bag in the car.September 26, 2026 – 10:09 AMMeanwhile, the gap to the four riders in the break is now at 2:19 with 140km to go, and the Dutch team is still controlling the front, followed by France.Tas moved through the team cars and is back in the pack.September 26, 2026 – 10:20 AMAnother crash but the riders went up and riding away very quickly with 131.7km to go.September 26, 2026 – 10:24 AMNews from the team on the ground in Montréal:Tereza Kurnická of Slovakia is actually a substitute for an injured rider, Nora Jenčušová - she's the team's soigneur and hasn't raced since 2022, except for fun on MTB.Tereza was apparently terrified of riding in a bunch this big, but she did race Worlds in 2021 as a junior so she's not a complete novice.But the countries need to enter riders to keep their qualifications for the coming years.The same will happen in the men's field tomorrow. Slovakia is putting a rider in who hasn't raced in years. September 26, 2026 – 10:26 AMBreak has 3:37 on the peloton as they head towards the Samuel-De Champlain Bridge, which could lead to more wind.Behind the Canadian team moved up to line up next to the Dutch team. Spain is also starting to move up.September 26, 2026 – 10:28 AMSeptember 26, 2026 – 10:33 AMOpened in 2015, the Samuel-De Champlain Bridge is 3.2km long, and replaced the old Champlain Bridge which was opened to traffic in 1962.The new bridge provides a multi-use pathway to pedestrians and cyclists, and three nesting boxes for peregrine falcons are installed along the bridgeThank you for coming to my Ted talk - back to racing.September 26, 2026 – 10:37 AMThe peloton is using the wide road on the bridge, happy to keep the pace steady, for now.The four riders in the break - Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria) and Beatriz Rosso (Portugal) - have 4:26 on the peloton as they exit the bridge onto the island of Montréal.September 26, 2026 – 10:39 AMStoyanova is falling of the pace in the break while Rosso also seems to be in trouble.September 26, 2026 – 10:40 AMThe women are heading towards the 13.4km circuit, which features four key climbs. The first comes soon after the finish line with the Voie Camilien-Houde, a 1.67km ascent averaging 7.4% and reaching a maximum gradient of 10%.Next is Chemin de la Polytechnique, 790 metres at 6%, including a punishing 200-metre section at 11%. The riders then face Avenue Pagnuelo, a 534-metre climb averaging 7%, topping out around the 9km mark.The final challenge is a 600-metre drag at 4% up Avenue du Parc to the finish.It is the same circuit that the previous categories faced on Thursday and Friday. The elite women will tackle the circuit eight times.September 26, 2026 – 10:41 AMBreak now down to 2 riders: Quinn and Edseth have 4:26 with 117.8km to go.September 26, 2026 – 10:48 AMPace has increased at the front of the peloton as riders being dropped include Georgia Baker (Australia), Olympic champion Kristen Faulkner (USA)September 26, 2026 – 10:54 AMCrash. Paula Blasi (Spain) and Anna Hendersen (Great Britain) involved but get quicky back up.September 26, 2026 – 10:56 AMTwo riders in the break are: Marte Berg Edseth (Norway) and Natalie Quinn (USA) as they cross the finish line to start the circuit and see 8 laps to go.They have a lead of 3:31 . Pace is amping up in the peloton as they take on the first lap of the circuit.September 26, 2026 – 11:01 AMPeloton is racing to position themselves before the first time up Voie Camillien-HoudeSeptember 26, 2026 – 11:04 AMPoland's Kaja Rusz is one of the riders dropped, which could impact team leader Kasia Niewadoma-Phinney who is one of the top contenders. Poland started the race with 5 riders.September 26, 2026 – 11:05 AMCorrection: Faulkner was not dropped; she is still in the peloton.But Baker did pull out of the race, and that leaves the Australian team down to 3 riders.September 26, 2026 – 11:10 AMLieke Nooijen (Netherlands) is putting the hurt on the peloton on the climb, as more riders drop from the back.As we have seen in the previous races - juniors and U23s - this circuit is tough, and not many will survive at the front.September 26, 2026 – 11:16 AMStill the Dutch at the front, with Vollering only a few riders back. French and Italian team also present to prepare for the descent off the Polytechnique climb. Quite a few riders had trouble on the bottom right-hand turn onto Blvd Edouard-Montpetit in previous races.September 26, 2026 – 11:17 AMPuncture for Spain's Sara Martin, who gets assistance from her team car.As the start, leader Paula Blasi said that there was an illness going around the team.September 26, 2026 – 11:20 AMGreat Britain's Flora Perkins accelerates at the front, but the Dutch come back to the fore on the Polytechnique climb.September 26, 2026 – 11:23 AMA lot of riders down from the middle of the peloton. Riders from Sweden, Great Britain, Spain, Australia and USA involved.Defending champion Magdeleine Vallieres Mill was also involved.USA's Kate Courtney is asking for her team to get a new bike.Will provide more updates on which rider was impacted.September 26, 2026 – 11:28 AMStarting the 2nd lap, break of Quinn and Edseth see their gap reduced by half, down to 1:56.The peloton, first whittled down by the tough circuit and then decimated by the crash, was down to around 40 riders, with a large chase group of around 40 riders behind. Defending champion Vallieres, covered in road rash, is also trying to chase back with a teammate. September 26, 2026 – 11:31 AMKim LeCourt-Pienaar and Kate Courtney are in a small chasing group but they are over one minute behind the pack.Blasi, also involved in the crash, pulls out.September 26, 2026 – 11:46 AMMore riders have pulled out: Sigrid Ytterhus Haugset (Norway), Christina Schweinberger (Austria), Lauretta Hanson (Australia), and Caroline Andersson (Sweden).All the best to the riders that may be injured in that hard crash.September 26, 2026 – 11:47 AMThe gap continues to tumble for the duo off the front, down to 16 seconds as Nooijen continues to set the pace at the front of the peloton for the Dutch team. The peloton is still around 40 riders strong with 6 laps to go. A big group is chasing behind, at around 30 seconds back.September 26, 2026 – 11:50 AMEdseth is pushing ahead solo.The LeCourt and Courtney group with Evita Muzic (France), Alison Jackson, Grace Arlandson (USA) is around 1:30 from the peloton.September 26, 2026 – 11:53 AMDefending champion Vallieres Mill is still on her bike, crossing the line to start the third lap, nearly 7 minutes down with one teammate with her, Adele Normand.September 26, 2026 – 11:56 AMLast rider from the break, Edseth, is caught with 76km to go as attacks fly off the front.Behind, a chase group with Amber Kraak, Lauren Dickson, Sarah Gigante, Monica Trinca Colonel, Mavi Garcia and more are working hard to close the gap, of around 20 seconds, to the peloton.September 26, 2026 – 11:59 AMFive riders from the chase group almost connect with the peloton on the Polytechnique climb, as the attacks at the front have calmed down.The commissaires have pulled all the cars in between all the groups. September 26, 2026 – 12:04 PMAnd the 5 riders finally join the peloton with 71km to go after a long chase. Garcia put in massive pulls to make that happen.Gigante is a few metres off the back. The Australian returned to racing after over a year away, and only has one race in her legs this year.September 26, 2026 – 12:09 PMThe 47-rider peloton, still with Nooijen and the Dutch team setting the pace at the front, crosses the line and sees 5 laps to go. Germany's Franziska Koch is close to the front, behind Vollering. September 26, 2026 – 12:11 PMThe Kim LeCourt group, which has swelled to 12 riders, is 1:48 down. Canada's Olivia Baril is 2:29 back with Courtney a further 30 seconds.September 26, 2026 – 12:14 PMHuge crowd is cheering on the riders on the climbSeptember 26, 2026 – 12:18 PMGreat Britain's team leader Zoe Bäckstedt is dropped on the Camilien-Houde climb, but chases back onto the pack on the descent.The 22-year-old claimed the silver medal in the ITT earlier this week.September 26, 2026 – 12:20 PMMagdeleine Vallieres Mill waves to the crowd as she crosses the line and pulls out of the race with teammate Adele Normand. Hugs her teammate, as the right side of her body is ripped out.September 26, 2026 – 12:22 PMAttack by Spain's Mireia Benito with 61km to go. Italy's Sara Casasola and Germany's Antonia Niedermaier jump onto the move. But they are brought back.September 26, 2026 – 12:26 PMWith 60km to go, Luxembourg’s Nina Berton attacks, and gets a quick reaction from Riejanne Markus (Netherlands).The Dutch team want to control while other nations are starting to launch riders off the front, However, France has not tried anything yet, and continue to follow moves. September 26, 2026 – 12:27 PMBig move by Great Britain, Koch responds immediately.And France finally attacks with Cedrine Kerboal accelerating. She looks over her shoulder and sees the peloton on her wheel.Ana Vitória Magalhães of Brazil tries her hand but is reeled back in.September 26, 2026 – 12:31 PMOver three hours of racing done, and still 53.6 kilometres to go as the peloton starts lap 5 of 8.Koch and Niedermaier chatting, with Liane Lippert on their wheel.September 26, 2026 – 12:33 PMFrench team launches another attack as Maëva Squigan hugs the barrier, while Noemi Rüegg (Switzerland) does the work to close this down, giving a respite to the Dutch team.The Swiss team swings off, leaving the Dutch team to do the work.September 26, 2026 – 12:36 PMSquiban has 21 seconds on the peloton led by Karlijn Swinkels (Netherlands). Swinkels knows exactly what Squiban can do, and how good a descender she is, as they both race for UAE Team L’IMAD.September 26, 2026 – 12:42 PMAnother crash involving a few riders: Pfeiffer Georgi (Great Britain) and Eleonora Gasparrini (Italy).September 26, 2026 – 12:46 PMColombia's Paula Patiño attacks from the right side of the road and gets a few metres, but that move only lasted a few minutes.September 26, 2026 – 12:47 PMThe French team had someone on the side of the road with a whiteboard message for Squiban. With no race radios, it's a simple way to give information to a rider.September 26, 2026 – 12:52 PMSquiban is well known for her solo raids, as she won two Tour de France Femmes stages in 2025 by taking a flyer.The 24-year-old, who took her gloves off, has a gap of 46 seconds with three laps to go.The Dutch team is still setting the pace at the front of the peloton, down to 35 riders.September 26, 2026 – 12:54 PMPuck Pieterse ramps it up on Camilien-Houde with Vollering on her wheel, dropping riders such as Backstedt, Kopecky, Faulkner, Benito and more.September 26, 2026 – 12:56 PMAfter cracking the field, Pieterse swings off, and Vollering attacks, catches Squiban briefly and continues on solo with 38km to go.Elisa Longo-Borghini is trying to chase back. September 26, 2026 – 12:59 PMNiewadoma-Phinney, Longo Borghini in the chase group along with Pieterse. Marlen Reusser brings up another group to reinforce the chase.September 26, 2026 – 1:02 PMVollering goes into time trial mode, already with 22 seconds on the 8-rider chase group.The chase includes Italy's Elisa Longo Borghini, newly crowned time trial champion Marlen Reusser (Switzerland), Polish duo of Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney and Dominika Włodarczyk, and three French riders Maëva Squiban, Celia Gery and Juliette Berthet. And Puck Pieterse is sitting on while her team leader Vollering is off the front.September 26, 2026 – 1:06 PMReusser is doing most of the work in the chase group, but there is no sustained effort in the group other than the time trial world champion. Gap to Vollering is 22 seconds.September 26, 2026 – 1:08 PMLongo Borghini attacks from the chase group, Gery goes with her with 30km to go. The two are cooperating to bring back Vollering. September 26, 2026 – 1:10 PMReusser counters once Longo Borghini and Gery are brought back. They can see Vollering up ahead but this circuit is tricky as we saw in the previous races. September 26, 2026 – 1:12 PMVollering is on a mission but has not gained the amount of time she may have hoped for. With two laps to go, and 26.8km to go, the Tour de France Femmes champion has 20 seconds.Longo Borghini is leading the chase, flicks the elbow and Reusser comes through. September 26, 2026 – 1:16 PMOn terrain that suits her, the Camilien-Houde climb, Vollering gains a few seconds.Reusser is back at the front of the chase. Some of the riders don't have the legs, or refuse to do hard pulls to close the gap down.September 26, 2026 – 1:18 PMDominika Włodarczyk is dropped from the chase on the climb. Gery is suffering. Longo Borghini and Niewiadoma-Phinney are pulling away on the climb, and now on the hunt to catch Vollering.September 26, 2026 – 1:20 PMVollering's gap stabilized at 18 seconds.September 26, 2026 – 1:22 PMChase regroups with Longo Borghini, Niewiadoma-Phinney, Reusser and Berthet. Pieterse is still there and weirdly allowed to roll through, probably slowing things down.September 26, 2026 – 1:24 PMBig fight in the chase group to try and separate the group.Niewiadoma-Phinney attacks on Polytechnique climb, with Longo Borghini trying to stay on her wheel with 38km to go. Berthet goes deep to catch back onto the pair.September 26, 2026 – 1:26 PMPieterse and Reusser are chatting. Reusser shakes her head, one can imagine she is saying something like 'you do the work if you want to get back on'September 26, 2026 – 1:30 PMAnother big acceleration by Longo Borghini, closes the gap down to 10 seconds. Niewiadoma-Phinney takes over to shave more seconds. Vollering still has a few metres, and forcing the other two worked hard to catch her.Berthet is trying to ride herself into the wheels, while Reusser has dropped Pieterse.September 26, 2026 – 1:31 PMThe connection is made inside of 16 kilometres to go. Vollering stays at the front with Longo Borghini and Niewiadoma-Phinney on her wheel.Berthet also makes it back the group, making it four at the front. The French rider is a trade teammate of Vollering on FDJ United-Suez.September 26, 2026 – 1:34 PMMassive attack by Longo Borghini as the bell rings for the eighth and final lap. The Italian is racing her 15th road world championship.Vollering is forced to chase with Niewiadoma-Phinney on her wheel.Reusser is about 15 seconds back.September 26, 2026 – 1:37 PMLongo Borghini has 4 seconds as she climbs Camilien-Houde climb for the last time.Berthet is distanced as Niewiadoma-Phinney sits on Vollering's wheel.September 26, 2026 – 1:40 PMAnd it's back together, with 11.5km to go for Longo Borghini, Vollering and Niewiadoma-Phinney.The Dutch rider ups the pace again with 200 metres to go on the climb, dropping Longo Borghini who is paying the price for that attack,Niewiadoma-Phinney refuses to work with Vollering,Behind Berther and Reusser are together.What a race! Who will win the rainbow jersey?September 26, 2026 – 1:42 PMVollering keeps looking back at Niewiadoma-Phinney, but the Polish rider is refusing to ride.If they play games, Longo Borghini could come back, she is 11 seconds back.September 26, 2026 – 1:43 PMFinally, Niewiadoma-Phinney takes a pull at the front with 7.5km to go, but not for long. September 26, 2026 – 1:45 PMHuge crowds cheer on the riders as Longo Borghini is only 6 seconds back as the two at the front keep on looking at each other.September 26, 2026 – 1:46 PMUsing her descending skills, Niewiadoma-Phinney takes the front on the descent, going 65 km/hr.September 26, 2026 – 1:49 PMNone of the riders in the lead three have been elite road champion. The pressure is on. Vollering accelerates, trying to drop Niewiadoma-Phinney, while Longo Borghini can't quite close the gap.Niewiadoma-Phinney goes around and attacks on Polytechnique but not able to drop Vollering.September 26, 2026 – 1:52 PM2 kilometres to go as Vollering is back at the front with Niewiadoma-Phinney on her wheel.Longo Borghini is 15 seconds back and Reusser a further six seconds.September 26, 2026 – 1:53 PMNiewiadoma-Phinney takes the front under the red kite. Looks behind her, and Vollering goes through.Vollering also looks behind her to see Longo Borghini who is not giving up.September 26, 2026 – 1:56 PMNiewiadoma-Phinney launches her sprint early, sprinting side by side with Vollering fastest to the line as Niewiadoma-Phinney cramps up in the finale.Vollering finally wins the road race world title for the first time in her career.Longo Borghini uses the barriers to get close to the duo but it wasn't enough and takes bronze. Reusser is fourth and Berthet takes fifth.September 26, 2026 – 1:59 PMHere is how the top 10 shaped up after more than four hours of racingTop 10 - elite women road raceDemi Vollering (Netherlands)Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney (Poland)Elisa Longo Borghini (Italy)Marlen Reusser (Switzerland)Juliette Berthet (France)Puck Pieterse (Netherlands)Dominika Wlodarczyk (Poland)September 26, 2026 – 2:05 PMSeptember 26, 2026 – 2:09 PMWhat a race! A perfect advertisement for the Grand Prix cycliste de Montréal to add a women's race. The GP is raced on the same tough circuit around Mont-Royal.September 26, 2026 – 2:14 PMMake sure to read our post-race report on all the action while also keeping an eye on our homepage for the latest reactions and news. September 26, 2026 – 2:19 PMSeptember 26, 2026 – 2:37 PMIt is a first-world title in a row for the world's best women's cycling right nowSeptember 26, 2026 – 2:39 PMAnd that brings our penultimate live report for the World Championships in Montréal, Canada to a close. There is one more race to go: the elite men road race on Sunday. Will it be as edge-of-your-seat exciting as the elite women’s race?We’ll find out tomorrow morning starting at 9am local time.

item.title: A new twist for 30th year of Tour de Langkawi with trio of summit finishes that will have sprinters fighting to 'just survive'
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: A win is never all there is at stake in any race, but somehow at Le Tour de Langkawi it's a fact that doesn't quietly tap away in the background but leaps into the spotlight with a deafening roar. For a start, the long-running Malaysian event offers a rare chance to launch a career, while for others it is a last chance to save it for those riders yet to secure a contract for 2027. Then there are the crucial points at stake in the never-ending relegation battle, and its current position near the end of the season also often makes it a farewell tour for riders who have decided, or had decided for them, that it is time to step away from the sport. Altogether, it delivers the ingredients for a heady and emotion-filled, no-holds-barred battle with the backdrop of an exotic location plus a hot and humid climate which will have the riders raising a sweat even just walking to sign in at the start of each of the eight stages from September 27 to October 4. The race, which pulls together teams from the WorldTour, ProTour, Continental ranks and national teams for a race in a region which prizes its high-level UCI race opportunities, given they are limited, will also be throwing some new elements into the mix for its 30th edition this year.Usually the sprinters are in focus for much of the event, with a decisive climbing day in the mix that is often decisive in the General Classification battle, but this year there are three summit finishes to add fire to the overall fight, with organisers pointing to the race as among the toughest editions ever. It's a welcome move for the riders who enjoy the uphill, but the sprinters and others who may not be pure climbers but perhaps thought they may be able to hang in there for one day and have a shot at the GC. "Yeah, the organisers have done a good job of removing any hope for riders like myself of having any chance at the GC with how hard they've made it this year," quipped Aaron Gate (XDS-Astana), the winner of the final stage of last year's race.Sprinter Fernando Gaviria (Caja Rural-Seguros RGA)was even more succinct when asked what he thought about the trio of climbing days: "For me it's just survive."These will be days when the fast men become allies in the autobus, looking to beat the time limit rather than enemies, getting through so they can battle once again. Those among the key sprint contenders include last year's three-time winner Matteo Malucelli (XDS-Astana) – although we are yet to see if there may be any impact in stage from a training crash on Saturday that saw him quickly subbed out of the pre-race media conference line-up as his teammate Gate was subbed in. The potential sprint competition includes the five-time Giro d'Italia and two-time Tour de France stage winner Gaviria along with Modern Adventure's Riley Pickrell, though the Canadian rider is unfortunately one teammate down even before the race has even begun. Leo Hayter posted on social media that while he made the journey to Malaysia, he then discovered that he had pericarditis, so he has had to end his season. There is only one flat stage for the sprinters – from Shah Alam to Kampar – before the climbing begins, with the introduction of the new ascent of Gunung Jerai as a shorter but steep finale for stage 2. Stage 3 then delivers an early category 2 challenge, which could well be a break launching point, though it flattens to give the fast-finishers another potential chance in Kuala Kangsar.But the next two stages, with their long and challenging ascents to the finish line, are unquestionably all about the climbers. These include new revelation speed-skater turned cyclist Jasch Lennart (Tudor), Jan Castellon (Caja Rural-Seguros RGA), Nicolas Breuillard (Total Energies), Harold Martín López (XDS-Astana) and Jonathan Caicedo (Wheeltop Rotor Chengdu), who won the 2.Pro ranked Tour of Magnificent Qinghai in July.When the Ecuadorian champion, who in 2020 won a Giro stage on top of Mount Etna, was asked if he considered himself the favourite, Caicedo said, "My goal is a top ten finish in the race. I was training very hard in Ecuador; I think I'm good for the race, I'm ready for this."Stage 4 heads into the Cameron Highlands – where overall race winner Simon Carr claimed victory in 2023 – with the road steadily ascending for more than 40km to the line. Then there is a second stage in a row that is finishing with a Hors-category climb, as the race on stage finishes in the Genting Highlands, which is an ascent that crowned Max Poole as the winner in 2024.From there, stage 6 from Pandan Indah to Rembau offers some early category 3 challenges but flattens out after the first 20km, while stage 7 from the vibrant historical location of Melaka to Batu Pahat has nothing in the way of obstacles for the sprinters but the final stage to Putrajaya delivers a category 3 climb 50km from the line which could prove a launching point for an attack as the very last chance at a tour filled with riders looking for them unfolds.*Cyclingnews attended Le Tour de Langkawi on an invitation/media package from the race that included travel and accommodation. In line with our editorial standards, our coverage is independent and was not subject to review, approval or influence by the organiser or any sponsor; no favourable coverage was promised or given in return.

item.title: Northeast Faces Wind, Rain and Coastal Flooding
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg News meteorologist Craig Allen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nor'easter will bring waves of heavy rain and strong winds to the Northeast, along with risks from falling trees, localized flooding and dangerous coastal conditions. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Allen says coastal flooding could affect Long Island, the Jersey Shore, Connecticut and Massachusetts as rough ocean conditions persist through multiple high-tide cycles. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Mideast geoeconomics lead Dina Esfandiary tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a protracted Iran war, marked by cycles of escalation and pauses in fighting, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'A top three would be a hole-in-one' - McNulty, Simmons and Jorgenson give USA the best chance in decades for World Championships road race
item.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: The last American rider to win on the same course in the Grand Prix de Montreal, Brandon McNulty, sees the 2026 Worlds as his country's best shot at their first elite men's title since 1993."It's the best team I think the U.S. have had," McNulty told after the time trial on Sunday. "Of course there's going to be crazy good guys from all the nations, so we have our work cut out. I think we have a good team to race super aggressively and try to do something.There's a ton of strong guys that we still don't think have ever really beaten before. So it's gonna be hard, but we have numbers to at least play our cards well."The US team have McNulty, Matteo Jorgenson and Quinn Simmons as their protected riders. After Neilson Powless withdrew from the team due to illness, according to USA Cycling, he has been replaced by Riley Sheehan, who had felt snubbed by being named as a reserve. The team also has Kevin Vermaerke, Artem Shmidt, Larry Warbasse, and Sean Quinn. McNulty, third in the GP de Montreal two weeks ago with Simmons, who finished fourth just behind, are the top contenders, together with Jorgenson, who was second overall in Tirreno-Adriatico this year, and remains one of the country's top one-day race competitors. caught up with Team USA's sports director for the elite men's race, Mike Creed, who seemed realistic about the team's chances based on the superstars they're up against - even in the absence of Tadej Pogačar, who is out because of his crash in the Vuelta a España. Isaac del Toro (Mexico), Remco Evenepoel and Wout van Aert (Belgium), and Paul Seixas (France) will be hard for the US riders to beat."[A top five] might be the best we can do, depending on who's in front," Creed tells . "We're more capable of getting a medal with multiple guys at this race than ever. That doesn't mean we should, or it'll be a failure if we don't."Matteo [Jorgenson] was there and thereabouts at Québec [eighth -ed.] and he's going to have to have better legs on the day. I'm not writing him out, but he's acknowledged that. Kevin [Vermaerke] came out of the Vuelta - he spent like the last 10 days in the breakaway, so like if he's a little cooked, it wouldn't be the most surprising thing in the world. So, if you figure that we have two guys who don't have question marks over them about their form. [It will be] clear we made a mistake if we don't have anyone in the first 15," he added before giving a golf metaphor. "Par is top 15, top 10 is like a birdie, and I think top five, top three is a hole-in-one."Obviously, it's a World [Championships], and you want to dream for the sky, but the fact is just because we are excited to be in North America and have a really good team doesn't mean that Wout and Remco aren't who they are. I love the idea of a Rocky movie triumph - I'll be the happiest guy in the world if that happens, but I don't want these guys to make moves based off of a cinematic background score."Creed was able to watch the Under-23 Women and Junior Men's races to see how the races played out on the quite arduous Montreal circuit - 13.4 kilometres long with two significant climbs and very little flat roads in between."It was similar to how I thought it was going to play out, not because I'm incredibly smart or anything, but just because the course runs a certain way. In the women's race, when [the breakaway] had two minutes, you're like, 'They're not really making any inroads,' and then when the bigger-name riders went, they got it down to 30 seconds really, really quickly," says Creed."Then, [it was the] same thing in the Junior Men's race. Unless it's a bigger group than three or four - it has to probably be like six or seven - for it to be that dangerous. Otherwise, it's just really hard to be out there by yourself or in a small group, with the fast downhills where the pack can really pick up a lot of speed - free speed, accelerating out of the turns. All these things that just really add up when you're solo or in a small group."There's no room for error - you can't get caught behind; you don't want to chase. It's not like Remco [Evenepoel] in Montreal, where he bridged to the leading five or six by himself. Even as strong as he is, he got there, then on the next lap [he paid for it]. So it's not a climb that you want to do a lot by yourself unless everyone else is already smoked."You saw in the Women's Under-23 race, the Australian girl [Felicity Wilson-Haffenden], she just was dropping bombs on people. And even then, she went just a little too early, and it kind of gassed her."In the Junior Men's race, Spain's Benjamín Noval attacked out of the bunch with 45km to go, reached the breakaway, then dropped them to go solo for almost two laps. It's the kind of scenario that a time trial world champion like Noval can pull off - and one Evenepoel can realistically do, too. How can the US team keep that from happening?"By making sure that the guys are as fresh for that attack as possible," Creed replies. "You can't make Remco not Remco. You can only just prepare yourself the best you can for that move, and then hope for a little bit of luck after that. It's not always fun to have that in a race plan; you want as little 'hope' as possible in a race plan. But ultimately, I think there's probably two other guys that eight times out of ten can follow Remco from bottom to top."That would be Seixas and Del Toro."Even then, they've got to have a fairly decent race leading into it. I think McNulty, six or seven times out of 10, is going to be able to stay with that, especially if he has a clean race. Simmons about the same, Matteo more or less the same. Because there is a drafting section in the middle of the climb. It's steeper at the bottom, then you can draft in that main part, so..."Although the team had not yet held their strategy meeting at the time of our conversation, Creed says the riders were all "on the same page and really open to playing the cards close to their chest"."I think we really want the best possible result. We all do."In order to get their best shot at a world title, Creed says the race has to be as hard as possible before the end of the 110-kilometre run-in from Brossard."I think McNulty and Quinn and Matteo are very durable riders, and the more time on the pedals for everyone, the better. It could be windy at the start and there are some open sections. I don't think it would be something where you'd get Qatar-style echelons - it won't split to like 30 [riders] and then keep it all the way to the line. But it could just cause some being on the pedals and a little bit more stress than most people would generally like for a 270km race."The run-in to the circuits is not exactly straightforward. It's got a good little bump in it; it could be crosswinds over the bridge... I might be tempting fate saying that, because maybe we'll end up on the bad side of something, but I think as much of a shit-fight of a race as possible suits us. It eliminates a lot of variables."Along with Belgium, Creed says the French team, who are fully behind Seixas, will be dictating the race."I would be surprised if France made the climb easy once," he says. "I'm sure France wants as many hard climbing kilometres as humanly possible. They probably don't want Wout to go up the road, and then have them chasing while Remco sits on. That's probably not a very enviable position. Belgium is very blessed in having a Remco because he can go with 60 km to go; he can also go with 15 km to go."The earlier an attack, the easier it will be to chase down for nations that have full squads, but it depends on who ends up in a breakaway."If Remco's not bridging to a powerhouse like a Mads Pedersen or Stefan Küng - a guy who's going to go pull-for-pull with him and just help carry him along in all the high-speed downhill and flat sections - if he goes up there with a bunch of people who are just swinging, not helping him, then maybe [he can be chased down]," says Creed."We hope the race gets chaotic, and we're able to go in some moves mid-late and not use a lot of energy - have the race come up there, and we have guys in both selections. Then we end up having numbers, and then we can play from there."It's such a delicate fine edge because you want to slip into moves rather than make the moves, and you want the people that you slip in with to be people who can carry a lot of the weight. You want some Mads Pedersen-type to go with Quinn - that's a good move. It's not necessarily a good move if Quinn and Del Toro go, because then it would be a better position to sit on, and Quinn's not going to want to sit on."Unlike in the past, Creed says riders from other countries aren't usually colluding because they share the same trade team the rest of the year."They don't do that anymore - they used to, but I think those days are gone. If you're on UAE, I think you're probably well-paid enough. That could probably happen if you had a guy who was like a straight-up domestique."You even saw last year in Kigali, Pogačar didn't wait for [Del Toro] - he kind of sat up for a second, and was like, 'Hey, you good?' And then was like, 'Oh, all right, well, I got to go, bye!' At the end of the day, they're there to win races, right?"If anything, maybe it would be like the social pressure - if you got into a two-up breakaway - of trying to pull just as hard as your teammate because you guys have a friendly rivalry. Like last year with Del Toro, maybe he should have sat on a little bit and been like, 'Bro, I'm wrecked,' but you know, you get excited and stuff. But no, that's not a problem. I mean, Quinn's teammates with Mads, you know, like, unfortunately everyone's got teammates."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. Subscribers get unlimited access to exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!

item.title: Tesla’s big electric truck faces an even bigger infrastructure challenge
item.author: Aarian Marshall, wired.com
item.content:encoded: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has insisted investors think of his electric automaker as a robotics and autonomous vehicle company now. He’s targeted a $20 trillion valuation—nearly four times the value of market leader Nvidia—on that premise. But his Tesla team was in Sparks, Nevada, on Thursday to focus on, well, an electric vehicle: the long-awaited Tesla Semi.The Semi concept first rolled onto a Tesla event stage in late 2017. Nearly a decade later, Tesla officially launched high-volume production at a livestreamed but invite-only event at the company’s factory. It targeted a niche audience: the cost-conscious people who manage large trucking fleets. A handful of them, all men, trooped across the stage to be thanked for their orders to a pulsing techno beat.“It’s going to be, really, a driver’s truck. It’s like a sports car in truck form.” Musk said in a pre-taped video played during the evening event. (Musk, for years the ringmaster at Tesla’s circus-like events, skipped his second vehicle debut in a row; he was attending a White House China State Dinner featuring President Xi Jinping.)

item.title: The truth behind Donald Trump’s ‘biggest oil deal in world history’

item.content:encoded: The US’s oil deal with Venezuela faces multiple legal and logistical problems, including questions about whether it can be implemented Donald Trump has long coveted the oilfields of other nations and declared an agreement with Venezuela to be “the biggest oil deal in world history”. But the agreement, reached after the US seized Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro, is almost certainly doomed to collapse amid a wide array of legal and logistical issues, a Guardian investigation has found.The US president first mused about taking oil from Iran in 1987, when he told ABC’s Barbara Walters that Iranian attacks on American shipping during the Iran-Iraq war required an extreme response. “Why couldn’t we go in and take over some of their oil, which is along the sea?” he asked. Over the ensuing years, he has returned frequently to the idea that the US should seize oil from other countries after military conflict, from Libya to Iraq.Continue reading...

item.title: Amazon’s Ring wants to replace local WhatsApp groups. It’s a recipe for curtain-twitching disaster | Imogen West-Knights
item.author: Imogen West-Knights
item.content:encoded: Do we really want a slick digital message board overseen by Amazon? It’s the neighbourhood nonsense we treasureRing, the Amazon subsidiary of camera-enabled doorbells fame, wants to be an even bigger part of your neighbourhood. Next month in the UK, it will be launching Neighbours, a community app that seeks to replace the now traditional neighbourhood Facebook or WhatsApp group. It will be available inside the Ring app, free to everybody, including people without Ring products, and will include a community requests feature wherein the police can ask for footage from residents living near reported crimes, who can then choose whether or not to share it.My first thought was that this is curtain-twitching culture gone mad. If you must have a Ring doorbell (and my instinctive feeling as someone without one, a feeling I will no doubt have until I get one and decide it’s great, is that it’s narc-coded behaviour) then: OK. But does Amazon need to be in charge of a digital village messageboard too?Imogen West-Knights is a writer and journalistContinue reading...

item.title: Yankees news: Schlittler, Fried still both in play to start Game 1
item.author: Jake Devin
item.content:encoded: MLB.com | Bryan Hoch: Cam Schlittler put the finishing touches on his Cy Young season Thursday night against the Rays. It wasn’t his sharpest start, Schlittler needing 70 pitches to navigate three innings, but it put his ERA on the season at 1.95, the lowest mark by a Yankee starter since Ron Guidry posted a 1.74 ERA in his legendary 1978 season, and the third-lowest ERA in franchise history. It’s also the lowest ERA by an American League starer since Justin Verlander’s 1.75 ERA in 2022, which won the future Hall of Famer* his third Cy Young.*Incidentally, Verlander is making his final career start today in Detroit.New York Post | Dan Martin: Speaking of Schlittler, you’d expect a pitcher of his stature to be a shoe-in for Game 1 of a playoff series. However, the Yankees are considering saving him for Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series. Max Fried could start Game 1, on extra rest, and thus also give Schlittler an extra day of rest before the Yankees embark on what they hope will be a long postseason run. Schlittler would have enough rest to start Games 2 and 5 of a potential ALDS regardless of whether he pitches Game 1 or 2 of the Wild Card Series. Is it possible the Yankees are overthinking it? Yes, admits pitching coach Matt Blake, but these are precisely the things the club’s staff is paid to overthink.Whichever way the Yankees line things up, the good news is that their excellent rotation means that they’ll have an ace-caliber talent going every night. As an aside, Andrés wrote up this debate for earlier in the week, and that’s worth a read if you haven’t checked it out yet.The Athletic | Evan Drellich and Andrew Marchand: Drellich and Marchand report on the looming lockout, and one mark to look out for next year: 60 games. Apparently, if MLB misses 60 or more games in the 2027 season, the league’s national broadcast contracts would extend an extra year, into 2029. That introduces an interesting wrinkle into the owners’ calculus when it comes to this round of labor negotiations. On the one hand, the league would still receive their negotiated dues as part of their deals with their broadcast partners. On the other, extending those deals another year means the league can’t negotiate new national deals for another year; the league is likely seeking to earn a hefty raise on their next round of national contracts. The league also wouldn’t get paid in 2029 under this scenario. SNY | John Flanigan: Ryan Weathers threw a live bullpen session yesterday, facing hitters including Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham. Aaron Boone said Weathers was up to 96 mph on his fastball, though called his control a little “scattered.” According to Boone, Weathers is on track to be an option during the playoffs, but it’s unclear if the Yankees will put the left-hander on the Wild Card roster. Carlos Lagrange also threw to hitters at Yankee Stadium yesterday, though it’s unlikely he’ll be on the playoff roster soon. Boone said he isn’t in play for the Wild Card roster and Matt Blake threw cold water on the idea of him debuting in the playoffs, though it still remains a (remote) possibility that Lagrange could factor into the Yankees’ plans later in the postseason if the team advances and Lagrange’s rehab continues to go well.

item.content:encoded: New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devicesDrones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested.In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.Continue reading...

item.title: How drawn-out saga of Manchester City’s alleged cheating came to this
item.author: David Conn
item.content:encoded: Club’s ruthless approach was always at odds with their public image and this inglorious story has further to runThere is no episode in English football’s history that even resembles a precedent for the epic Manchester City disciplinary drama, which encapsulates the modern game at breaking point. Here was a grand, stoic old club, taken over in 2008 by Abu Dhabi royalty and mega-funded to imperious success, then crowned serial champions by a league simultaneously pursuing charges of monstrous financial cheating.On Friday sources confirmedthat saga, in which Pep Guardiola’s expensively constructed City teams won five Premier League titles and the Champions League during the years since the investigation began in December 2018, culminated in guilty findings on almost all of more than 100 charges.Continue reading...

item.title: Yankees pitchers strike out a whopping 17 to split Orioles doubleheader
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: It wasn’t exactly a meaningful game, but the Yankees projected a much better image in the nightcap against the Baltimore Orioles and won it 6-3 after losing the first game in ugly fashion. New York’s pitchers certainly brought the strikeout stuff for this one, as Ryan Yarbrough, Will Warren, Brent Headrick, John Schreiber, and Alexander Cornielle combined to punch out 17 — tied for a team sign high among standard nine-inning efforts with a gem led by Cam Schlittler’s 13 on June 19th against the Reds.The Yankees’ record is now 93-68 with one regular season game left. If the weather holds off (no guarantees there), they have a shot at matching last year’s 94-68 record, which is frankly not bad because their best player, Aaron Judge, only suited up for 66 games. This game actually started as a pitchers’ duel, with Orioles’ starter Brandon Young and Yarbrough trading zeroes for the first 2.1 innings. The lefty departed after 49 pitches, but did not allow a run despite surrendering four hits and a walk, fanning five.The Yankees brought in Warren with one out and a runner on first, which represented a nice training scenario ahead of his expected bullpen role in the Wild Card Series.As it turned out, Warren was amazing, even though he allowed a double in that same inning that could have produced a run for Baltimore, and covered 3.2 scoreless frames while conceding a mere three hits and racking up seven strikeouts. He will finish the regular season with a nice 3.92 ERA and just over a strikeout per inning.The Yankees finally got to Young in the bottom of the fifth. After two outs, Austin Wells walked and crossed home thanks to Ryan McMahon’s RBI double.Young pitched a very solid game, completing five frames in which he conceded a single run on two hits and three walks. He whiffed six and finished the game and the season with a 3.56 ERA.The Bombers extended their lead in the bottom of the sixth against the O’s bullpen. Spencer Jones singled in Heliot Ramos, aided by a fielding error by right fielder Rece Hinds. Later in the inning, Anthony Volpe (playing shortstop with George Lombard Jr. getting a rare rest) hit an automatic double that plated Luis García Jr. and Jones to make it a 4-0 ballgame.Headrick replaced Warren in the seventh and surrendered the Orioles’ first run. With the bases loaded and one out, Leody Taveras hit a sac fly to bring in Pete Alonso. Ramos and García would hit consecutive RBI singles in the bottom of the inning, though, and the Yankees were up 6-1.Cornielle entered for his MLB debut, and was promptly greeted by a Dylan Beavers homer to right, making it a 6-2 ballgame. The rookie got into some trouble after the long ball, putting two men on base before getting the first out. He then surrendered a very long RBI double to Taveras that just missed the stands, as the O’s trimmed the Yankees lead to three runs.Cornielle then shook it off and struck out the next two hitters to end the ballgame on a high note. Ben Rice went 2-for-3 with a double, a walk, and a run scored, and McMahon went 2-for-4 with a double, a run, and an RBI. Volpe plated two, and Wells walked twice and scored once.The Yankees are supposed to wrap up their season on Sunday against the Orioles, starting at 3:20pm ET. Elmer Rodríguez has been announced as New York’s starter. However, the nor’easter that forced this doubleheader in the first place has led to some bad forecasts for Sunday, so it’s very possible that Game 162 gets nixed. We’ll find out soon enough! Stay dry out there.

item.title: New York Yankees vs. Baltimore Orioles: Ryan Yarbrough vs. Brandon Young
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: After CC Sabathia’s No. 52 retirement ceremony and a rather forgettable Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader, the New York Yankees will take the field again and face the Baltimore Orioles in the nightcap. The Bombers already know that they will host the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card round, and the O’s are already eliminated from playoff contention.As a result, this is merely a tune-up game for New York, but that’s certainly not insignificant ahead of another edition of their rivalry with the Sox. Brandon Young will take the ball for Baltimore, trying to wrap up a solid year. The 28-year-old followed up his mediocre 57.2-inning cameo last year with a very solid campaign in 2026, with 151.2 frames of a 3.62 ERA, a 4.53 FIP, and 127 punchouts. He is not a star, but did more than enough to win a long-term spot on the O’s staff.The Yankees, with that series against their bitter rivals looming, didn’t announce their starting pitcher for Game 2 of the doubleheader until just about 10 minutes ago. Long reliever Ryan Yarbrough gets the nod for his second start of the season; he last pitched on Tuesday. His only other start of 2026 was the second game of another doubleheader against the Dodgers, when he went 2.2 shutout innings back on July 19th.Yarbrough is obviously not built up length-wise to go deep in this one either, but the expectation is that Will Warren will pitch a couple innings as preparation for the playoffs. He last pitched on Sunday in Arizona. Big things were expected from Warren this season, and while he didn’t exactly develop into an ace, he has been steady as a rock with a 4.02 ERA in 152.1 innings. A team would take that from its No. 5 starter any day of the week. David Bednar, Brent Headrick, and Paul Blackburn can only pitch so much, so Warren could certainly make a positive impact in the ‘pen.Also keep an eye on the bullpen for Alexander Cornielle. A career minor-league signed before the season, the right-hander made 16 starts for Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre and was activated to the big-league roster between games with matinee starter Brendan Beck optioned. If he appears tonight or Sunday, it will be his MLB debut.From this point forward, everything the Yankees do on the field will be with the Red Sox in mind, so don’t expect an all-out effort from those expected to be on the Wild Card Series roster. Indeed, there isn’t a ton of overlap between the Game 1 lineup and the Game 2 starting nine, as the Yankees are avoiding using too many players if possible. Indeed, the Game 1 infield went Paul Goldschmidt/José Caballero/George Lombard Jr./Anthony Volpe from first to third, and Game 2 has Luis García Jr./Jazz Chisholm Jr./Volpe/Ryan McMahon, with Volpe giving Lombard a spell by shifting over to his familiar six for the first time since his early-August demotion. Cody Bellinger tags in for Heliot Ramos in left, while Ramos shifts to right and Amed Rosario takes a seat. Austin Wells will catch and Spencer Jones is the only one starting the same position in both games, in center.: Yankee Stadium – Bronx, NY: 7:30 p.m. ET: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 Gotham Sports App, MLB.tv (out-of-market only)

item.title: Yankees flop after CC Sabathia ceremony, lose to Orioles
item.author: Matt Ferenchick
item.content:encoded: With nothing left to play for on either side, the Yankees vs. Orioles series opener was somewhat overshadowed with the number retirement ceremony for CC Sabathia that took place before the game. The expected bad weather tomorrow forced a doubleheader today and moved the ceremony up to this afternoon as well. The short notice change led to the stands being emptier than anyone would like, but it was still a nice ceremony for the now-forever Yankees’ No. 52. Old friends Derek Jeter, Andy Pettitte, Dellin Betances, and Chris Young joined in the festivities on the field, alongside Sabathia’s family.On the field, things could’ve gone better.Making something of a spot start with the doubleheader and the Yankees planning ahead for the postseason, Brendan Beck started for the Yankees. Not that it was something the Yankees were considering, but Beck didn’t particularly make a case to be a last-second playoff roster addition. In his five innings, he allowed seven runs on six hits and three walks, including two home runs. The bullpen wasn’t particularly lights out following him, allowing the Orioles to build up a big lead.The Yankees’ offense was always going to be up against it considering that fact, but they didn’t do much. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers mostly kept the Yankees in check as Baltimore kept adding on. The Yankees could only plate one run from their eight hits, dooming them to a 10-2 loss in the first game of the doubleheader.On the mound, Beck started things off with a couple scoreless innings. However, Baltimore got on the board in the third. Beck nearly got through the inning again, but issued a two-out walk to Dylan Beavers. That came back to haunt him, as Pete Alonso did a Pete Alonso thing and homered to put the O’s in front.An inning later, Beck loaded the bases after walking two and allowing a single. Christian Franklin then dropped in a single, plating another Orioles’ run. After a force out got a runner at home, Beavers took Beck deep for a grand slam, putting Baltimore well in front.The Yankees got on the board themselves in the bottom of the fourth. Heliot Ramos reached with a triple, aided by center fielder Colton Cowser misplaying the carom off the wall. Amed Rosario followed that with an easy single to score the Yankees’ first run.Baltimore got that run back a short time later, thanks to an outfield miscue of the Yankees’ own. With reliever Yerry De los Santos in for the Yankees, Jeremiah Jackson hit a ball to deep right-center. The ball just got over the glove of Spencer Jones and took a fortuitous bounce past him. Jackson managed to race all the way around and beat the throw home for an inside-the-park homer, the first one in the Bronx in a dozen years — coincidentally with today’s honoree on the mound against Wil Myers. Alonso added a more conventional homer in the seventh in that it went over the fence, but it was unconventional in that it was an absolute bomb, 471 feet away.Honestly, I can’t even be mad at that one. Baltimore would tack on one more run to get to double digits for the game. Paul Blackburn and David Bednar got their work in as expected, and we now won’t see them again until the Wild Card Series.The Yankees did get one run back after Spencer Jones singled in the bottom of the ninth and eventually came around to score on a Paul Goldschmidt sacrifice fly. Ben Rice struck out looking to end it.One pretty disappointing thing to come out of the game was the play of the offense. Yes, the game didn’t actually mean anything, but the Yankees did send out the likes of Goldschmidt and Rosario and their theoretical “lefty” lineup. Them not doing much on offense isn’t what you would want to see considering that the Red Sox Wild Card Series lineup is now locked in and Boston has a bunch of left-handed pitchers they can throw at the Yankees.The second game of today’s doubleheader is set to begin at 7:30pm ET, which New York just announced. Brandon Young will go for Baltimore, while the Yankees will counter with Ryan Yarbrough, with Will Warren expected to provide relief work in anticipation of his playoff role.

item.title: Can Trump ever be wrong? His pick to lead FDA refused to say.
item.author: Beth Mole
item.content:encoded: Heidi Overton, President Trump's nominee to lead the Food and Drug Administration, went before the Senate health committee Thursday, facing questions about her stances on vaccines, flavored vapes, birth control, and abortion, among other issues. She spent nearly two hours stonewalling senators, even on softball questions.Overton, a physician with a doctoral degree in clinical investigation, is currently the deputy assistant to the president for domestic policy. She previously worked at a conservative think tank and has taken a clear stance opposing abortion, raising obvious questions about her objectivity. The FDA is currently reviewing the safety of the abortion pill, mifepristone, despite extensive data showing it is extremely safe.Overton also notably stood behind President Trump at a press conference in August during which Trump falsely called the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine "quite lethal." He further claimed that vaccine doses for infants are "like the size of a soda bottle," and called for the MMR vaccine to be split into three separate immunizations, despite no evidence of benefit from such a split and no such individual immunizations being available in the US.

item.title: Court rules Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic for refusing to enable Claude features
item.author: Jon Brodkin
item.content:encoded: A US appeals court today approved the Department of Defense's blacklisting of Anthropic technology. Judges decided the Trump administration had authority to blacklist Anthropic for withholding certain AI features from the military even if Anthropic had no malicious intent.In a 2-1 ruling issued by the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, a panel of judges said the "case raises profoundly difficult questions about the appropriate military uses of an almost unimaginably powerful new technology." The US "raises the deeply sobering prospect of overly constrained AI models shutting down unexpectedly and thus causing important military operations to fail. Anthropic raises the deeply sobering prospect of unconstrained AI models hallucinating inappropriate targets for lethal military force," the ruling said.Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth "must determine how best to balance the competing risks," the court said. "In doing so here, the Secretary did not transgress any limits on his authority under the Supply Chain Security Act or the Constitution. Accordingly, we deny the petitions for review." The same court previously denied Anthropic's emergency motion for a stay in April.

item.title: Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements
item.author: Jeremy Hsu
item.content:encoded: Tesla’s pivot from making electric cars to humanoid robots is facing challenges because of complex robot hands and disgruntled employees pushing back against training their robotic replacements. The struggle to scale up production comes as Tesla CEO Elon Musk has bet the company’s future on AI and robotics.As someone who frequently makes claims that fail to materialize, Musk has described the Optimus humanoid robot as potentially “the biggest product ever” during Tesla’s second-quarter 2026 earnings call. But he also acknowledged that making an autonomous humanoid robot capable of handling many different tasks is “one of the hardest things to solve”—and now extensive reporting by The Information has revealed multiple complications that Tesla is trying to tackle while developing general-purpose robots and scaling up for mass production.

item.title: UCI Road World Championships: Alejandra Neira takes junior women's road race title from five-rider escape in Montréal
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: Alejandra Neira gave Spain their third gold medal of the UCI Road World Championships, winning the junior women's road race in a hotly-contested five-rider sprint in Montreal.Neira patiently waited until the final 150 metres to put in a massive turn of speed, leaving Matilde Rossignoli (Italy) in her wake to take silver, while Anja Grossmann (Switzerland) claimed third.After the dual titles from Benjamín Noval in the junior men's time trial and road race, Neira's gold medal represents the future of Spanish cycling."I can't believe it. It's the best day of my life," Neira said. "I can't believe that I'm the World Champion. It's incredible."Last year, it was Neira's teammate Paula Ostiz who won the title. Now it's her turn. "Paula is a big, big friend, also teammate, and to be the World Champion after her, wow, incredible."Neira was part of a three-rider escape along with Grossmann and Rossignoli, but the pair were caught in the final three kilometres by Maria Okrucińska (Poland) and Mirthe Mons (Netherlands), which shook her confidence a bit."When the other riders arrived, I lost a little bit my confidence, because Maria is a really good sprinter. But I tried to keep on her wheel, and then when I saw that I have to pass, I went."Grossmann finished fourth in the junior women's time trial, so found redemption with a bronze medal, though she said the final 26km were a challenge after a missed water bottle."I think the the last two laps were pretty intense and pretty tough because the Spanish girl attacked at the feed zone and I didn't catch my bottle there, so I rode like two laps without my bottle," she said at the post-race press conference. "That was hard because I got pretty bad cramps. But I think I worked really on my mental strength, and that just kept going. I'm not the best sprinter, but I just try to to sprint as best as I can."This year's route for the junior women measured 5.6km longer than the Kigali route and included a little more climbing, a total of 1,614 metres of elevation gain. Canada, Great Britain and Spain came with five riders each, giving them an edge with numbers.It was not until the second lap that the complexion of the peloton began to change, with riders falling off the back rather than anyone accelerating away. Spain, Australia and Poland were represented at the front.With just under 45km to go, French rider Sidonie Vachet put a spark in the proceedings with an attack at the front of a fractured peloton. She opened a slight 16-second gap on the uphill to start a fourth circuit, marking the halfway point of the 80.4km race.Behind, Scout Wellmeier (USA) rode at the front with Lluna Jimenez (Spain), Eva Drhova (Czechia), the Australian duo Chloe Bowen and Neve Parslow, and Polish duo Maria Okrucińska and Amelia Szymańska, and another 31 riders packed into the peloton.Bright sunshine helped the temperatures rise as high as 24°C (76°F), the warmest afternoon of the championships so far, and riders took on plenty of liquids at the feed zone along the climb. Across the summit of the Camillien-Houde, Vachet relented to the pace behind and the race reset.Once across the Polytechnique climb and on the twisting city-centre streets of Montréal, Great Britain riders could be seen gathering at the front. But it was an acceleration from Colombia's Zara Sofia Lamprea that came on the approach to the Parc Avenue climb.Lamprea carried a 10-second advantage, with Wellmeier trailing in solo second. The reduced peloton of 35 riders began the chase with two laps remaining at 20 seconds.There was a crash at the front of the race under a heavy canopy of trees, with Lamprea and Wellmeier going down. Both were back riding quickly, but as they made the penultimate ascent of Camillien-Houde, the chase began closing down their effort.A group of 10 crested the summit, and Lamprea just a few seconds behind and Wellmeier farther back, now chasers. France, Spain and Germany each had two riders, with one rider each from the USA, Netherlands, Great Britain and Switzerland. Then on the back side of Mont Royal, more riders tagged along for a bigger group.Riders upped the pace to position at the front, passing crowds at the Polytechnique Montréal centre for science and technology, with a series of twisting turns on the descent causing riders to go wide on the course.With 18.5km to go, Nabyenka García (Mexico) was the next rider to put in an extra effort, gapping the field by 15 seconds quickly on a flatter section. The Mexican rider looked back several times, and finally kept on the accelerator to go alone.The bell lap rang with long shadows forming in the late Canadian afternoon, García still out front but only by 14 seconds. The curse of race leaders continued as she stopped for a mechanical, looking to reposition her chain, and was forced back in the peloton.Wellmeier, Vachet, Parslow, Orucińska and Lidia Castro (Spain) were setting the pace at the bottom of the final ascent. Mirthe Mons (Netherlands) pushed the pace at the front, which seemed to spur others to give it a go. Soon a trio were at the front - Anja Grossmann (Switzerland), Alejandra Neira (Spain) and Matilde Rossignoli (Italy) - and with 10km to go had 20 seconds on Okrucińska and Mons.With 4km to go, the trio weren't showing signs of working togehter, which allowed Mons and Okrucińska, the new world time trial champion, to edge closer in the chase. "Maybe we should have worked a little bit more together, so the other two wouldn't came back. But that's junior racing because junior racing is always a little bit more hectic and a little bit more without a clear tactic. I wanted to work together, but it was not my decision," Grossmann said later.With 2km to go, there were five to fight for three medals.Mons struck first on the final climb. Then mountain bike world champion Grossman passed, then Rossignoli, but it was Neira who went wide on the right side and took the victory.Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: How to watch Yankees vs. Red Sox in AL Wild Card Series: Start times, channels, and more
item.author: Dani Mohr
item.content:encoded: The MLB postseason is finally upon us, and the No. 4 seed Yankees are kicking things off by facing the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, just as they did in 2025. New York will end the season at least four games better than Boston, but as they say, all records reset to 0-0 come October — or very-late September in the case of the 2026 season.The Red Sox defeated the Cubs on Friday afternoon to officially clinch the No. 5 seed, meaning the Yankees will have home-field advantage by starting the postseason in the Bronx. They already knew they would be hosting, but it wasn’t yet official that they would face Boston. Per MLB’s Sarah Langs, this will be the seventh all-time postseason meeting between the Yanks and Red Sox, tied for the second-most common matchup in league history and trailing only the 12 famous Yankees/Dodgers World Series rumbles. New York and Boston have each won three series apiece in the playoff head-to-heads.You won’t want to miss all the action in the best-of-three series next week, with the winner advancing to face the Rays in the American League Division Series in a race for the pennant.Here’s all the information you’ll need to know to tune into every game this weekend. item.title: 'We gave it everything' - Aubin Sparfel ready to join Paul Seixas at Decathlon CMA CGM after Montreal Worlds disappointment
item.author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
item.content:encoded: Rising talent Aubin Sparfel ends his under-23 career in disappointment, having finished just off the podium in fourth place in the under-23 men's race at the UCI Road World Championships on Friday.The 20-year-old French rider came into the race as the big favourite, and was hoping to secure the rainbow jersey. Now, he will turn his attention to joining compatriot Paul Seixas in the WorldTour with Decathlon CMA CGM after spending four seasons growing through the team's development ranks. "We are a little bit disappointed, but we gave it everything," Sparfel told "Of course, we were here for the victory. It's like that. I'm super proud of the team and proud of myself. I had a super amount of pressure on me after the win last week [Grand Prix de Wallonie], and I felt like I could finally dream about winning."Sparfel had another successful season with the Decathlon CMA CGM Development programme, kicking off the year with an overall victory at Le Tour de Bretagne Cycliste, taking sixth overall at Boucles de la Mayenne-Crédit Mutuel, fourth overall at Giro d'Italia Next Gen, and winning a stage of the Tour de l'Avenir. He capped off his season with a victory at the one-day Lotto Grand Prix de Wallonie, showing top form heading into these Worlds and setting himself up as one of the favourites."Of course, I learned a lot this year. I won a lot, and I think I'm ready to step up. It was a super good season, and I can thank everyone around me. My team, the France team, my coaches and my family. It was a super good year," he said.During the under-23 men's road race, Sparfel joined a chase group that also included silver medallist Héctor Álvarez (Spain) and bronze medallist Jesper Stiansen (Norway) in a failed effort to bring back new world champion Ashlin Barry (USA).Despite his disappointment in finishing fourth, Sparfel praised Barry on his winning performance. "Ashlin was super strong," Sparfel told . "We knew that he could win this year, but we did everything we could as a team, and we were super strong as a team. "In the last two laps we did a lot with the other guys from the big favourites, but in the end, we arrived in the race for second place - it's like that."Sparfel will now turn his attention to racing alongside Seixas, fourth overall in the Tour de France this year and a favourite in the elite men's road race on Sunday. The two riders are among the nation's most promising talents on the WorldTour."I will go to the WorldTour, so I will no longer race in the under-23s. I've ridden on every team with Paul since we were juniors and know him really well," Sparfel told ."I will race for Decathlon next season, and we will see what we can do. I will speak with the team about my race program, but I'm proud of my under-23 racing season, and now I will focus on elite for next season."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia.
